function: Learned AP-UE pairing (Dueling DQN), bandwidth and power allocation (attention-driven multi-agent actor-critic) maximizing communication rate minus weighted sensing CRLB in cell-free ISAC (p. 5-6)
system: Downlink cell-free massive MIMO ISAC: 15 APs (8 transmit, 8 receive antennas), 8 single-antenna UEs; TDD, 20 MHz; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9)
method: Hierarchical multi-agent RL: Dueling DQN commander for pairing, attention-driven multi-agent actor-critic workers for bandwidth and power; centralized training, decentralized execution; trained by environment interaction (p. 5-8)
data_channel: Own simulator: channel with distance-based large-scale fading, steering vector and Gaussian term [33], 0.2 km square, random UE positions and demands; no dataset (p. 3, 9)
test_conditions: Default 15 APs, 8 UEs, random positions and demands; sweeps of K, N, larger scales and an imperfection test; retraining per setting not stated (p. 9-13)
baselines: All learned: HMARL [55], H-DQN, SAC, DDPG, SA2C [56]; no classical or non-learned baseline (p. 10)
metrics: Average system utility score, per-UE sum data rate CDF, per-UE CRLB CDF, execution time, CPU-AP signaling load, convergence, resource utilization (p. 10-13)
complexity: Big-O training (43) and testing (44) complexity, plus execution time 3.71 ms higher layer and 0.107 ms per agent lower layer (Table II) (p. 9, 11)
q1_support: p. 3: "The channel coefficient between the k-th AP and the n-th UE at time slot t is modeled as [33]", a custom steering-vector plus Gaussian model with unspecified large-scale fading; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "we evaluate the system performance under the influence" of pilot contamination, phase noise and channel aging, with training conditions not stated; p. 13: "three cases with increasing difficulty levels, ranging from" K = 30 to K = 65, without saying a trained policy is reused.
q3_support: p. 10: "Five state-of-the-art benchmarks are considered:" HMARL [55], H-DQN, SAC, DDPG and SA2C [56] are all learned methods; no optimization, random or fixed allocation baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "Accordingly, the overall computational complexity of" Algorithm 1 per training episode is given in (43), and testing complexity in (44); p. 11: "requires 3.71 ms at the higher-layer controller and" 0.107 ms per agent (Table II).
notes: Included as area 5: the AP-UE pairing is user association (above the physical layer) but is learned jointly with bandwidth and power allocation that serve rate and CRLB, i.e. resource allocation for ISAC; reviewer should confirm. q2: p. 11 claims policy generalization, yet the commander state and output and the worker state depend on K and N (p. 6), so the sweeps over K and N and the scales of Table III appear to need retraining, which the paper does not say. q3 is 0 only because every benchmark is a learned method. Tables II and III and Fig. 11 were read from the page images.
